hints: Look at the $\text{COO}$ group in the middle of P, that is the signature of an ester, so think about how esters are normally made.
Split P at the ester link: the $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}$ part comes from a 3-carbon acid and the $\text{OCH}_2\text{CH}_3$ part comes from a 2-carbon alcohol.
Name that 3-carbon carboxylic acid and that 2-carbon alcohol, then pick the pair that would join together with loss of water to give P.
walkthrough:
**Recognise P as an ester**

P is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOCH}_2\text{CH}_3$. The $\text{COO}$ in the middle tells you it is an ester.

Esters are made by esterification:
$$\text{carboxylic acid} + \text{alcohol} \rightleftharpoons \text{ester} + \text{water}$$

**Split the ester into acid and alcohol parts**

Think of breaking the $\text{CO-O}$ bond. The acyl side keeps the $\text{C=O}$.

Acid part: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}$ gives $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$, which is propanoic acid. Alcohol part: $\text{OCH}_2\text{CH}_3$ gives $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$, which is ethanol.

**Write the formation reaction**

Putting those two together with concentrated sulfuric acid catalyst gives P:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH} + \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH} \rightleftharpoons \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOCH}_2\text{CH}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
So the pair is ethanol and propanoic acid.

options.A: Two carboxylic acids do not react together to form an ester. Esterification needs one acid and one alcohol, so this pair cannot give P.
options.B: Ethanoic acid ($\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$) with propan-1-ol ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$) would give propyl ethanoate, $\text{CH}_3\text{COOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. That is the wrong way round, with 2 carbons on the acid side and 3 on the alcohol side.
options.C: Propanoic acid provides the $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}$ fragment and ethanol provides the $\text{OCH}_2\text{CH}_3$ fragment. Together they form ethyl propanoate, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOCH}_2\text{CH}_3$, which is exactly P.
options.D: Two alcohols do not react together to form an ester. Alcohols can be oxidised or dehydrated, but ester formation requires a carboxylic acid partner.
